thread.title: Midday Update: Wall Street Braces for FOMC Outlook on Inflation

author: MT Newswires
title: Midday Update: Wall Street Braces for FOMC Outlook on Inflation
text:
Shutterstock photo Wall Street's major averages surrendered early gains and drifted into the red as defensive posturing before the Federal Open Market Committee concludes its policy meeting upstages strong quarterly results from component stock Apple ( AAPL ) and strength in the energy complex.
Investors shifted their focus Wednesday from the deluge of corporate earnings to interest rate policy, and more specifically, how the Federal Reserve will incorporate recent wage and inflation data into monetary policy. In the past, the Fed was committed to a 2% inflation target, keeping its foot off the brake to achieve that illusive level. But with the 10-year Treasury note doing the heavy lifting at 3%, the Fed can either chose to back off further increases, or commit to at least two more hikes this year.
On the earnings front, upbeat results from Apple helped mitigate damage to both the Nasdaq and Dow Jones Industrial Average. The tech giant beat Wall Street's profit and sales expectations even as iPhone X sales were below estimates. The stock raced to a 10-day high at the open, slicing through resistance at its 50- and 100-day moving averages.
On the other end of the spectrum was Snap ( SNAP ), which missed revenue and daily-active user estimates from Wall Street analysts. The company also reported a loss of $0.17 per share, though that was narrower than the $0.20 loss last year, and was in-line with expectations.
On the economic front, a survey from Automated Data Processing showed the private sector added 204,000 new jobs in April, beating the consensus estimate of 190,000, but down from a revised 228,000 increase in March.
Bullish corporate results and manufacturing data buoyed European bourses with Germany's DAX closing 1.51% higher, following by solid gains for the Euro-STOXX and UK FTSE-100.
Crude oil was up $0.26 to $67.51 per barrel. Natural gas was down $0.05 to $2.76 per 1 million BTU. Gold was down $0.70 to $1,306.30 an ounce, while silver was up $0.27 to $16.40 an ounce. Copper was up $0.03 to $3.06 per pound.
Among energy ETFs, the United States Oil Fund was unchanged at $13.61 with the United States Natural Gas Fund was down 1.49% to $22.49. Amongst precious-metal funds, the Market Vectors Gold Miners ETF was up 0.25% to 22.39 while SPDR Gold Shares were down 0.01% to $123.72. The iShares Silver Trust was up 1.12% to $15.41.
